item.title: Finally figured out streamers…
item.description: I’ve messed around with streamers on and off over the years without much luck, so I spend a lot of time drifting dries and nymphing.Today I decided to set up an old 8’ 6wt with a short stiff leader, and tossed a 3” sculpin into a deep pool I’ve fished unsuccessfully dozens of times.

item.title: Charged aggressively by beavers at night. Lessons where learned
item.description: Went fishing in a beaver meadow, got into some beautiful brookies. One of the biggest iv ever caught. A real hog for only being 12". Then night time rolled around…. and I was hoping to target some browns, wading through this section of river. It contained 5 dams and a large beaver lodge.

item.title: Booked a “master fly fishing guide” and he took us trolling instead
item.description: I booked a 4-hour master fly fishing guided experience at a country club in Ireland. We got on the boat and got put to the river and the guide pulls out two trolling rigs with bass pro swim baits. We trolled back and forth along the same stretch of river for four hours and didn’t catch a thing.

item.title: Seward Alaska
item.description: Good afternoon, my girlfriend and I are going to be in Seward for a few days before heading over to the kenai.While we are in Seward we would like to try and target Silvers or Dollys on a fly rod. Are there any good areas or rivers we should check out for this? Any tips would be greatly appreciated.

item.title: Can we talk shop about double nymph rigging?
item.description: I don’t have any friends or anyone else that fly fishes and also don’t have a nearby fly shop to chop it up with either. I’ve been a pretty successful fly angler on my own but I’ve been questioning my rigging lately and just curious about it.

item.title: The Guy In Brown
item.description: By Brian Kozminski From a distance, whether mowing the lawn, tending to the animals, or cutting wood, I can recognize the “Fa-Thump, Fa-thump, Fa-Thump” amplified rotation of the tires and diesel engine working up the motivation to travel up the long hill a mile away from our house.

item.title: First fish on a fly rod

item.title: Protect the Head of Your Nymphs with Thin Skin
item.description: The more durable a fly, the more fish you can catch on it and the longer the life of the fly will be. Making a point to tie and purchase your flies with durability in mind will save you time at the tying bench and keep a little extra cash in your wallet. Nymphs in general are the work horses in our fly boxes.

item.title: Big sky Missouri
item.description: Been in Montana for like 3 days now, tried changing it up from the Gallatin to some smaller mountain streams and it was the right choice, huge brown trout out of a stream only a few feet and my first ever cutties, fishing here is a million times easier than anywhere I fish in Va on Nc

item.title: Gar on the fly
item.description: Just landed a prehistoric missile with teeth on a fly rod on a fly i tied. Apparently “delicate presentation” still works on a fish that looks like it swam out of Jurassic Park and forgot to evolve. My tippet is currently in therapy.

item.title: Casting Large Flies on 10wt is terrifying
item.description: Sooo…. any tips for long casts with large flies on a 10wt? I’ve been at Smith Mountain Lake all week fishing for bass, mostly wading out from the banks around docks. Long casts for hoppers and poppers has been fine, small minnow patterns okay… but casting large clousers has been terrifying.

item.description: Permit fishing is as exacting as it gets. item.title: Farm Waters
item.description: By Ethan Smith If we want clean water we need to pay farmers to clean it up. What? Yes, let’s pay farmers a premium over the current farm subsidy program to help keep our rivers clean! That sounds crazy right? Well it isn’t, let me explain. The farm bill and its subsidies are currently clean water’s worst enemy.

item.title: You Can Mouse Just About Anywhere

item.title: Muscle Tension in the fly Cast: Video
item.description: You can’t make a good fly cast if you are tense, but muscle tension is necessary, at the right time. Do you squeeze the grip of the fly rod when you cast? At some point, you should be. I’ve seen a lot of casters who use a white knuckle grip when they cast. You can’t make a good cast that way.

item.description: By Bob Reece After twenty five years of fly fishing for freshwater species, I recently threw my first casts into salt water. As is always the case, hindsight is 20/20. While I had plenty of success, there are several things that I wish I would have done prior to my first saltwater trip. I’ve always been a huge proponent of practicing your casting.

item.title: The Eat
item.description: Fly fishing is all about the eat. I remember a day floating the Snake River, about two decades ago. There was a freshly fallen tree jutting out at ninety degrees to the bank. Deep in the safe confines of its branches was a nice cutthroat, rising steadily. “It’s an impossible fish,” my guide told me but I can’t resist a rising fish.

item.title: Listen to the Fish
item.description: Sometimes all fly fisherman need to do to find success when their not having luck is slow down, and take the time to listen to the fish. Trout can’t speak to us in words, but they do often provide us with subtle clues from their behavior that can help us catch them. That is, if we’re paying close enough attention to pick up on them.

item.title: The Double Figure 8 Loop knot
item.description: Loop knots give your fly superior action in the water. There are several good options for creating a loop knot but tied in heavy salt water tippet, like you use for tarpon, most get quite bulky. In the first of three videos on better salt water knots, Capt. Joel Dickey shows us how to tie the Double Figure 8 Loop Knot.

item.title: The Economy of Wraps in Fly Tying
item.description: THE HALLMARK OF WELL-TIED FLIES IS NATURAL PROPORTION. This is never more true than when tying tiny trout flies. Trout are visual feeders and there are three primary criteria that a fly must meet to elicit a positive response. It must match the natural in size, color and profile. Of these three, the hardest to match in tiny flies is profile.

In autumn it even hosts salmon when it migrates through here.

item.title: Tenkara Presentation, Really “Fishing” The Fly
item.description: By Tim Harris One fly, but many ways to fish it. In a play of words, it is said that “tenkara” means “ten colors” since the kanji is the same - テンカ ラ. This means ten tenkara fishers have ten different styles of fishing. This could be that they use ten different flies or that they fish ten different techniques.

item.description: I was undergunned for this fish. Was casting a 4wt mid flex rod with a PMD dry + emerger combo to 12-16” rainbows that afternoon.It was a careful 8 minute fight in a drift boat trying to keep a barbless #18 fly in the front tip of her jaw.I estimate it was 1 in 10 chance of landing it.

item.title: Patagonia’s Endless Summer
item.description: It turns out there is a cure for winter. The sky is blue. The sun is warm. Red stone cliffs rise above deep green water. Rolling hills covered in sage brush, or what looks like sage brush, roll uninterrupted as far as the eye can see. Twenty-inch brown trout rise out every green pocket to eat big bushy dry flies.

item.title: You guys ever have this happen to you?
item.description: Was fishing today and hooked into a solid brown. Fought him for a bit. Saw him flash - he was a biggun. But mid fight he just glued himself to to the bottom and didn’t move. My rod was cranked and I was at the absolute limit of my tippet trying to use some lateral pressure to pull him to the side but he wouldn’t budge.

item.title: From Lakes to Lagoons: Your Saltwater Survival Guide
item.description:
Transitioning from freshwater to saltwater fishing might feel like learning to ride a bike again—except this time, you’ve got waves, salt, and maybe a shark or two. The insight from fellow anglers shows that while the fundamentals of casting and retrieving remain, the nuances of saltwater fishing require some tweaking. Whether you’re fishing the beaches of La Paz or the jungles of Costa Rica, adapting your skills is crucial.
